Dickens attacked workhouses. When does knowing that earn marks?
One printed scene, a question on the whole play. Where do you start?
'This is a metaphor' earns almost nothing. What makes it analysis?
identity-poetry: From cursing his fate to scorning kings. What changes his mind?
A calm sea on a moonlit night. Why does he hear only sadness?
In a hospital bed, he calls himself master of his fate. How?
A woman sings at a piano. Why does a grown man end up in tears?
Two war poems, a century apart. How do you compare, not list?
relationships-poetry: A father calls his hope a 'sin'. Why blame himself for loving?
Her eyes are nothing like the sun. Love poem or insult?
She promises to 'count the ways'. Can love really be measured?
He'd court her for centuries. So why won't he wait at all?
She's buying poison. Why does she want to watch it being made?
She begs to be remembered, then says forget her. Why?
He pictures her old and alone. Love poem or warning?
conflict-poetry: 600 men ride into a deadly blunder. Why does Tennyson say 'Honour'?
A cricket match and a desert battle. Why the same words?
He shot a man he'd have shared a drink with. Why can't he say why?
A recruiting poem calls war a game. What does that hide?
No bells, no prayers, no coffins. How are these dead mourned?
He expects to die in the war. Why doesn't he care who wins?
A love sonnet in a Conflict anthology. Where's the conflict?
macbeth: A brave hero in Act 1, a 'dead butcher' by Act 5. What went wrong?
Macbeth argues himself out of murder. Why does he do it anyway?
She begs spirits to 'unsex me here'. So why does she crack first?
The witches never tell Macbeth to kill. So are they to blame?
Macbeth sees a dagger, then a ghost. Are they real?
Why does killing a king make horses eat each other?
Verse, prose, rhyme: why does Shakespeare change how people speak?
romeo-and-juliet: The Prologue gives away the ending. Why would Shakespeare do that?
Romeo loves Rosaline, then Juliet, in one night. Fickle or changed?
Juliet obeys her parents in Act 1. By Act 3 she defies them. Why?
The greatest love story ever, or a warning about rushing in?
No one says why the feud began. So why does everyone keep fighting?
Meet on Sunday, wed on Monday, dead within the week. Why the rush?
The lovers only meet in the dark. Why is their love always light?
